What this check does — and its limits

The parser handles quoted commas, escaped quotes, multiline fields, UTF-8 BOM and CRLF/LF line endings. Headers are trimmed and case-normalised. Unexpected extra columns are disclosed and excluded from accepted exports.

All instances of a duplicate ID are held; no record is silently chosen as correct. Blank lines are ignored and counted. A failed file does not replace the previous successful run. This is a schema check, not proof of business accuracy or an immutable audit trail.

Metric definitions & reporting boundaries

Filters use the ticket’s opened date, including both endpoints. Backlog means Open or In progress. Overdue means unresolved with a due date before 26 October 2026; a ticket due on the snapshot date is not overdue. Ageing includes unresolved tickets only.

Summary cards and charts share the main filters. Selecting a card, status or age group narrows the register and its export; the summary remains a view of the base filters. Effort is input data, not elapsed time or a measured saving. No SLA, productivity or personal-impact claim is made.

Why I built this

Useful automation needs
visible checks.

This original demonstration connects two parts of business systems work: making inputs dependable, then making the result understandable.

It uses a bounded schema, explicit exception handling, reconciliation and traceable calculations. The demo is built with HTML, CSS and vanilla JavaScript; its data and outcomes are fictional.
